brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four full bases in a row (piece:0..3,0,0), each holding a shallow drainage bin (hex-bin-third-drain) filled with soil and planted (prop:1-4). Only these shallow bins fit, because the pipe passes through the bases. Open faces are capped and the joints between bases are bolted.

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell
requirements.evidence: Irrigation run run:run-1 passes straight through all four bases at level 0, under every bin, so each cell is on the line. Not checked: whether it stays watertight and how water actually gets from the pipe into each bin.

finish.summary: I built a four-cell planter in a straight row, with one irrigation pipe running through all four bases. The checks found no rule errors and no parts colliding, and all four plants are visible. There are 30 parts, and printing takes about 1,838 g of filament and roughly 45 hours. The configurator only checks how parts fit. It can't tell whether the run will hold water without leaking or whether the parts stand up to wet soil, because that depends on the material you print in and how the pipe is joined.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes

parts.use: Bolts a glue-in socket for 3/4 in pipe to any face that takes a bolt-on: a side flat, or the lid of a bolt cover. Solvent-weld a pipe into it with PVC primer...
